summary: Native Linux binary harvests Chromium credentials and cookies with embedded HTTPS client
details: The package ships a single Rust-compiled Linux x64 N-API binary (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) declared as the module's main entry, so it loads on require. Embedded strings show Chromium credential-store handling ('Found login for', 'Cookie.value when inserting', 'SQLITE_AUTH_USER') indicating the binary reads Chromium/Chrome/Brave/Edge Login Data and Cookies SQLite databases from the user profile under the installer's UID. The same binary embeds a full HTTPS client (ureq/rustls with RequireHttpsOnly, TLS handshake, session tickets) alongside host-fingerprinting primitives (gethostname, getifaddrs, network_adapters, /etc/lsb-release, /dev/disk/by-id/), the standard browser-credential-stealer shape with outbound exfiltration reachable from the same module. The destination host is not a plaintext literal, consistent with runtime construction/obfuscation. The package name mimics the @napi-rs per-platform native sub-package convention (`*-linux-x64-gnu`) but has no parent package listing it as an optionalDependency, and the version string `3.1.40-chrom-553-fix-undeletable-import-cookies-360-1784545605` embeds the payload description and a unix-epoch build tag consistent with a rapidly-iterated malware campaign.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
